_comment: Fragment 60 — D-105: the declared crossing git could not see; the handover that left no trace; the watch-list that excluded the newest instructions. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: D-105 — The Declared Crossing Git Could Not See
nodes.description: The fourth critic pass, performed on a separate turn against three committed decisions. Eight findings, none dismissed, five of them introduced by the corrections under review.
nodes.rationale: Every recorded pass has found defects in the pass before it, so the reject count rather than the pass rate is what this mechanism is measured by.

nodes.label: A Declaration No Audit Can Find
nodes.description: The commit gate matched its declaration keyword anywhere in the message body, while git parses only the final paragraph as trailers. Every declaration made since the gate was installed is invisible to git's own parser, including the one in the commit that installed it.
nodes.rationale: The gate has a blocking half and an auditing half, and only the blocking half ever worked. Its stated reassurance that bypassing hides nothing depended on an audit path that returned empty every time it was asked.

nodes.label: Ask the Tool That Owns the Format
nodes.description: The gate now obtains the trailer block from git itself rather than reimplementing the rule with a pattern, and rejects a body-only declaration with that specific diagnosis.
nodes.rationale: A reimplemented rule agrees with the original by coincidence and diverges silently. Telling an author to add a trailer is useless when they believe they already did, so the failure names the actual defect.

nodes.label: An Empty Report Is Indistinguishable From a Lane That Never Ran
nodes.description: A build lane held the sole commit permission for a full turn and produced no commits and no artifact, because its work order told it that its open backlog entries were the report.
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the repository distinguishes ran-and-found-nothing from started-and-failed from never-started. A backlog is not a handover, and using one as the other loses exactly the information a boundary exists to capture.

nodes.label: Report Especially When Nothing Happened
nodes.description: A turn now ends with an entry stating what was done, what was specified but not applied, and what is open. Nothing is an answer that must be written down.
nodes.rationale: A turn producing no work may mean the instructions were unclear, the environment was broken, or the turn never began. Silence records none of those and the answering side cannot tell them apart.

nodes.label: No Control Can Fail Against an Agent That Never Ran
nodes.description: The lane-state check verifies that exactly one lane holds commit permission, which is what it was built for. The boundary where a lane departed without reporting passed green.
nodes.rationale: The register records the absence instead, and that is a record rather than a gate. Presenting it as a gate would be the failure mode where a probe cannot fail.

nodes.label: The Departing Lane's Record Was Written by the Other Side
nodes.description: The register stated that no work was performed, presented as a neutral fact. It is the orchestration lane's observation of the commit log, not the build lane's report of its own turn.
nodes.rationale: This is the same structure as a resolution written by the side that wrote the fix, appearing in a new place three passes after it was first recorded. Attribution is the whole repair.

nodes.label: A Hard-Coded Watch-List Is a Filename Filter Wearing a Different Hat
nodes.description: The control installed to stop instruction documents going unread named two files, while two work orders sat unread — and one of them contained the very defect the pass went on to find.
nodes.rationale: An earlier gap was a filter that excluded a lane, a later one a filter that excluded the instructions, and this a list that excluded the newest instructions. The fix each time is to derive the set rather than enumerate it.
